CONCEPT: the personification of Salt — the lord of the Salt House of the Sodium Nation. A female character who IS that substance; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the substance’s traits, within the element’s own palette. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.
ELEMENT TRAITS of Sodium (Na) to carry in her design and the scene: a bright yellow flame that bursts when it touches water, cube-shaped salt crystals, the warm orange of sodium street lamps; soft silvery metal that must be kept under oil. Palette: sodium yellow, salt white, oil-dark silver, lamp orange.
HOUSE TRAITS of Salt: white cubic crystals, the white crust of a salt pan, coarse grain and sparkle; the gathered, nourishing side of salt. Palette: salt white, sea blue, sun gold, wood brown.
AGE: mid-twenties — a clear adult face; no facial lines.
SILHOUETTE: toned athletic-curvy, full-busted with rounded hips build; a long ponytail with curtain bangs; salt-white hair.
FACE — she must read as her own person at a glance, NOT the style's default pretty face and not a sister of the other characters: first impression — a cheerful, sunny openness; warm beige skin; softly square face; moderately sized, realistically proportioned eyes — narrow upturned eyes, level outer eye corners; soft rounded brows; small button nose; full heart-shaped lips; sky-blue eyes; a dusting of freckles across nose and cheeks.
WORLD — STEAMPUNK: around 1880, a street of gas lamps and a soda works: salt pans, evaporating basins, a sodium lamp glowing orange, brass and white crust. COSTUME (steampunk): late-Victorian industrial dress — a high-necked blouse with a waistcoat or a tailored tail coat, leather gloves, a work apron or utility belt with brass fittings, goggles hung at the neck or a small instrument as ornament; below, a short bustle skirt over riding trousers and laced boots; muted palette with the traits above as accents. No armor plates, no cape, no crown unless CONCEPT says she wears one; steam, pipes and gauges in the scene; no modern plastic, no sci-fi. LIGHT: hazy gaslight and a smoky overcast sky, unless TIME & WEATHER says otherwise. HAIR: her hair is worn exactly as SILHOUETTE says — loose, long or cut as named; do not pin it up into a bun or tuck it under goggles or a hat unless SILHOUETTE says an updo.
STYLE: Polished 2.5D game key art with clean linework, anime facial design that keeps each character's own facial structure, eye proportions and skin tone instead of one house face, layered cel-to-soft shading and crisp costume and prop detail. Use a vivid, readable silhouette and campaign-quality lighting.
EXPOSURE (bold): the high collar unbuttoned down to the sternum with natural cleavage, sleeves rolled above the elbow, a short bustle skirt showing the legs above laced boots; the waistcoat stays buttoned at the waist. Nothing slipped off. Chest and pelvis covered; no corset; keep the costume WORLD describes, material and palette.
OUTPUT: one character image that works as card art. Vertical 2:3 frame, full body with head and feet inside the frame with clear margins, face turned toward the camera (front or three-quarter). Standing, card-ready pose; the environment may be rich while her design stays fully readable.
EXPRESSION: crinkled lower eyelids, closed-lip smile pushing the cheeks up, brows relaxed.
BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose or the frame.
ONE FIGURE ONLY. No second character, no living creature, no logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border. No text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Na) and atomic number (11) — those two may appear readably (engraved, stamped, glowing or on a sign or label); nothing else is written.
ANATOMY: natural adult proportions, both hands drawn correctly as hands. No extra limbs.
